Changed rules. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes the `for` sentences of One expression per line and of the do: rule, references/macros.md, and the example under Use ETS for data many processes read, whose table options now sit on one line. Of the eleven listed rules only Use ETS is touched, in its example and not its prose, and no run here creates a table, so the sentence that decides that rule is the unchanged "A GenServer serializes access. When many processes read shared data, or update counters, put the data in an ETS table owned by a supervised process, and read and write it from the calling processes." All eleven are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/rate-limiter-baseline.json and rate-limiter-skill.json.

Design change that drives the Opus row. Opus-1 here is not last sweep's ETS design: it returned to the 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22-c design, a Supervisor over a PartitionSupervisor of GenServers, with every check a GenServer.call from MyApp.RateLimiter.check/1 to a Partition process. The earlier grades of that design set the standard: Pick the abstraction, Use ETS and Keep each process behind one module are violated. Without a :name option, as in 2026-10-22-b, Write GenServers that stay responsive is violated too. Partitioning removes the single bottleneck, so a reader who judged the two process rules by bottleneck alone would hold Pick the abstraction clean, but the table's row "Data read by many processes, or counters updated from many processes" names an ETS table, not a tier of processes. The other four keep every count in one GenServer's state, and three say so in their moduledocs (haiku-2 line 60, sonnet-1 line 82, sonnet-2 line 15), so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are 5 of 5.

Build a multi-line argument: 1 of 5 (opus-1), a judgment call. "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." decides opus-1 lines 86-88, a one-element child list whose one-line form is exactly 98 characters and which mix format leaves on one line (checked in scratch). The case's own record counted the same shape, a spread list that fits, in 2026-10-31 skill-sonnet-2, and the README entry on the ETS example says five options on one line "at 98 columns" is what the sentence asks, so 98 counts as fitting. A reading that exempts a child list, or a line at the very edge, makes opus-1 clean, the count 0 of 5 and the Opus tier clean. Library-client grades in this sweep left spread struct literals unflagged to match that case's previous sweep; here the same-case standard points the other way. The other four are decided by the opening sentence, "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list": no call takes a map, struct or keyword argument that spans lines. Opus-1's GenServer.call (lines 70-73) spans lines with tuple arguments, which 2026-10-22-c did not count; its one-line form also fits at 98, but the sentence speaks of literals, not calls. Return tuples are not call arguments (sonnet-1 lines 123-130, haiku-2 line 117, sonnet-2 line 97), as earlier sweeps held. No literal has more than six elements.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 2 of 5 (haiku-2, sonnet-1). Sonnet-1 init/1 is decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`". Haiku-2's else (lines 148-150) has a no-op clause and a catch-all, the shape 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-22-c counted. Opus-1's two-step with has a one-clause else that raises; it is held clean under "A large `else` block that maps errors back to steps is hard to follow", as 2026-10-22-c baseline-sonnet-2 held the same raise and 2026-10-31 order-report baseline-opus-1 held a one-clause else, with the catch-all listed under Match every expected shape. 2026-10-31 webhook-parser baseline-sonnet-1 counted a one-clause else as violated, so the standard is not uniform; counting it here would make opus-1 violated and the Opus tier violated. Sonnet-2's four steps are clean. Haiku-1 has only raising boot-time calls, so it is not exercised.
